conventions.convention: All filter arrays are real. Covariances are exact products LLᵀ of supplied rectangular factors; zero columns and rank-deficient factors are allowed. State and observation dimensions are positive, and the horizon may be zero.

Prediction pads the concatenated factor to at least the state dimension. Measurement places observations first, pads the measurement-noise factor to at least the observation dimension, and flips entire leading factor columns to make the innovation-factor diagonal positive.

Arithmetic uses the operationwise no-underflow model, left-to-right dot products, and stored exact orthogonal reflector representatives. Arithmetic failure returns a status; a rounded dense Q is not formed.

The local prearray bound uses Frobenius norms, requires qu<1 and ru<1 for each nonempty product, and permits the rational QR envelope only when 200qnu<1. Empty inner products contribute zero formation error.

The horizon recurrence uses operator norms and assumes ε_k≤μ_k/2 at every step, where μ_k>0 is a lower bound for the exact innovation covariance. Its conclusion is finite-horizon, with no uniform-in-time guarantee.

Positive semidefiniteness concerns the exact product of returned factor entries, not a separately rounded covariance materialization. Unstructured QR perturbations need not preserve independent-noise block structure. AC is inherited only for the statistical interpretation.
The subtractive-update witness uses binary precision p=24, round-to-nearest ties-to-even, and rounds the explicitly ordered expression P⁻−(KS)Kᵀ operation by operation.

load_bearing.statement: The finite procedure predicts by QR of a padded transposed factor array, updates by QR of the observation-first measurement prearray, solves the leading lower-triangular innovation system, and returns the trailing factor without a covariance downdate. Failure returns the first declared status; success records arithmetic and factorization completion only.

For real covariance factors of arbitrary rank and S=HP⁻Hᵀ+R≻0, exact reduced QR of the padded transposed measurement prearray gives L₁₁L₁₁ᵀ=S, L₂₁L₁₁ᵀ=P⁻Hᵀ, and L₂₂L₂₂ᵀ=P⁻−P⁻HᵀS⁻¹HP⁻. Solving L₁₁z=v gives L₂₁z=P⁻HᵀS⁻¹v.

For G∈R^{n×q}, q≥n≥1, successful scaled-Householder QR of the computed transposed array gives ‖LLᵀ−GGᵀ‖_F≤2‖G‖_F ε+ε², where ε=e_form+e_in+β_{q,n}‖Ĝ‖_F and β_{q,n}=(1+κ_q)^n−1. Under 200qnu<1, β may be replaced by 200qnu/(1−200qnu).
Let G,E∈R^{m×n} and set Ĝ=G+E. Then ‖ĜĜᵀ−GGᵀ‖_F≤2‖G‖_F‖E‖_F+‖E‖_F². The estimate is valid for all ranks.
Let q≥n≥1 and u>0. For β_{q,n}=(1+κ_q)^n−1 and C_{q,n}=200qn, if C_{q,n}u<1, then β_{q,n}≤C_{q,n}u/(1−C_{q,n}u).
If P=LLᵀ, Q=L_Q L_Qᵀ, and G=[FL L_Q] is padded to permit reduced QR Gᵀ=UR with UᵀU=I, then L⁻=Rᵀ satisfies L⁻(L⁻)ᵀ=FPFᵀ+Q, including zero and rank-deficient factors.

For S≽μI with μ>0, Frobenius block-error bounds e_S<μ, e_B, e_D, b≥‖B‖₂ and β=(μ−e_S)⁻¹, the perturbed innovation is positive definite, the gain error is at most e_Bβ+bμ⁻¹βe_S, and the Schur-complement error is at most e_D+2be_Bβ+b²μ⁻¹βe_S+e_B²β.
For nonsingular T∈R^{p×p}, p≥1, and residual r=Tẑ−y, ‖ẑ−T⁻¹y‖₂≤‖r‖₂/σ_min(T). If TTᵀ≽νI with ν>0, then σ_min(T)≥√ν.

concerns.concern: Proof steps 3.1 and 4.1 refer in prose to the inverse estimates of “steps 1.1–1.2”, but there is no step 1.2. The inverse-difference estimate is step 2.1, which both trailing tag groups correctly cite. The bounds themselves follow from steps 1.1 and 2.1.

Proof step 1.2 says “The upper-triangular innovation solve has finitely many rows”. The defined algorithm instead solves the lower-triangular system L̂₁₁ẑ=v̂ by forward substitution. This does not affect termination or the operation count.

seams_checked.note: Checked both page interfaces. This is a reading prerequisite: the square-root page imports no Riccati theorem or stabilizing-branch conclusion, and the Riccati page makes no reverse claim about this filter. Both distinguish unstructured numerical perturbations from preservation of model structure and require separate conditioning or stability evidence.
